ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 1.2:1 ratio of high-intensity (white/cream) to low-intensity (black/dark-gray) pixels across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-intensity region A (left lobe): broad white field from medial-bottom to lateral-upper, bordered by black stippling at the ventral-edge. High-intensity region B (right lobe): continuous white field extending from the medial notch area to the distal tip. Low-intensity region C: central vertical wedge at the peduncle intersection.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with a calculated angle of approximately 70 degrees and a vertical bounding-box depth of approximately 18% of the visible fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations visible along 80% of the trailing edge; peaks and valleys exhibit pixel amplitudes ranging from 3 to 12 pixels. A significant traumatic indentation is located on the left lobe trailing edge.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bi-lateral upward-sweeping curve; leading edges are concave-up, while trailing edges follow a generally convex curve modulated by high-frequency serrations.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-density cluster of high-contrast, textured pixel clusters at the distal extremity of the left lobe. Discrete white circular points are scattered along the dark trailing edge boundaries.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Faint, low-contrast dark vertical streaks (rake marks) visible within the white pigment field of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Major traumatic notch on the trailing edge of the left lobe. Significant irregular morphological protrusion and heavy texture on the far-left distal tip showing evidence of physical trauma or heavy colonization.
other_distinctive_markers: Extensive yellowish-tan bio-film (diatoms) covering approximately 40% of the visible white surface areas, primarily in the central lobe regions.
